new_statements.quote: 19. Wo hat jedes Wort seine Betonungs-Silbe, seinen Accént? Immer nur auf der Endsilbe.
new_statements.translation: 19. Where does each word have its stressed syllable, its accent? Always and only on the final syllable.
new_statements.citation: Schleyer, Johann Martin. 1889. Populär-katechetische Grammatik der Weltsprache Volapük, samt Schlüssel zu derselben. Konstanz am Bodensee: Verlag von Schleyer's Weltsprache-Zentralbüro.
new_statements.locator: p. 10, III. Buchstabenregeln, Frage 19 (ÖNB scan canvas 17)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (printed page number 10, ONB scan of 701532-A). Under the heading 'III. Buchstabenregeln.' the page reads exactly: '19. Wo hat jedes Wort seine Betonungs-Silbe, seinen Accént? Immer nur auf der Endsilbe.' -- verbatim as reported (the answer is set on its own indented line). Surrounding items: Frage 17 (no silent letters; every letter read, e.g. plied = pli-ehd), Frage 18 (one sound per letter), Frage 20 (Latin script only); nothing on the page qualifies or restricts the final-stress rule. Title page confirms the work: 'Populär-katechetische Grammátik der Weltsprache Volapük sámt Schlüssel zu derselben. Von ihrem Erfinder: Schleyer Johann Martin. Konstanz am Bodensee. Verlag von Schle…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Volapük falls invariably on the last syllable of the word (by design of the inventor, on the French model). Contemporary English grammars add that the hyphenated enclitic particles -li (interrogative) and -la (subjunctive) do not count: stress stays on the last syllable of the host word (Sprague 1888 p.2: 'The accent is always on the last syllable, exclusiv, however, of a syllable joined to it with a hyphen. -li and -la are the only syllables so hyphenized. Ex.: getòm; getòm-li? getòm-la.'; Post 1890 p.[1]: 'ACCENT. Is invariably on the final syllable, but non-coalescent endings are not regarded as word-syllables.'). Modern (de Jong 1931) Volapük materials state the same rule ('Words of more than one syllable are always stressed on the last syllable', Volapük Vifik lesson 1).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any source read.
new_statements.exceptions: Hyphenated (non-coalescent) enclitics -li (question particle) and -la (subjunctive) are outside the stress domain: getòm-li, getòm-la keep stress on the verb's final syllable (Sprague 1888 pp.2, 37, 39; Post 1890 p.[1]; Quick Look: 'unstressed interrogative -li'). Monosyllables trivially stressed. Adjacent vowels are separate syllables (laut = la-út, geil = ge-íl), so a final vowel in hiatus carries the stress (Sprague p.2; Omniglot's neai = [ne.a.'i]).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the orthographic/grammatical word excluding hyphenated clitics -li/-la; rule stated for words in general (citation and connected speech not distinguished). Constructed language: the rule is stipulated by the inventor, not observed.
new_statements.identity_note: Statement from Schleyer describes classical Volapük (Schleyer's original, 1879-1889 norm). The modern standard is Arie de Jong's 1931 revision (Volapük nulik); the open modern materials read (Quick Look at Volapük / Volapük Vifik, volapük.com) state the same final-syllable rule, so the rule is unchanged across both norms. Glottocode vola1234 covers both.

sources.note: p.6: 'The accent is always on the last syllable; thus tikele, to the thinker, is pronounced: tikelé (tee-kay-lay).' Introduction: Schleyer 'solved satisfactorily the problem of accentuation by adopting the principle of the French pronunciation, and always putting the accent on the last syllable.'

sources.note: p.2 'Sounds and letters': 'The accent is always on the last syllable, exclusiv, however, of a syllable joined to it with a hyphen. -li and -la are the only syllables so hyphenized. Ex.: getòm; getòm-li? getòm-la.' Later: conditional -la 'is written with a hyphen and the accent remains on the preceding syllable'; interrogative li hyphenated, 'The accent of the verb is unchanged.'
